_what: Every SHAPE a scout can drop off, and the named result `litkb.hunt.hunt` must end each one in. Driven by qc/test_litkb_hunt.py::test_ref_shapes (selectable with -k ref_shapes) against the worker database, with the registry client, the title resolver's client and the fetch all INJECTED — no test here opens a socket. The point is not that a hunt succeeds: it is that nothing ends in a traceback and nothing ends in a misclassification. Before 2026-09-20 `ref_kind` called every non-http reference a DOI, so the isbn and garbage rows below reached `admit_registry` and died at AdmissionError.

_columns.id: the row name; it is also the pytest parametrize id
_columns.ref: the reference exactly as the caller gives it
_columns.ref_scheme: what the caller DECLARES it is; null means the scheme is inferred from the shape
_columns.inputs: the other hunt() kwargs this row passes (title/author/year/extract/spend)
_columns.seed: a work seeded into the database before the hunt (scheme/value/state), or null. Seeding is how a row reaches a ladder rung without admitting anything: admission is tested by qc/test_litkb_p2.py, this file tests the front door
_columns.fetch: what the injected fetch does: explode (any call fails the test), html (200 + an HTML sign-in page), pdf (200 + a synthetic one-page PDF)
_columns.registry: none (a client that answers 404 to everything) or title_gate (the frozen Crossref search body of qc/fixtures/litkb_title_gate_wrong_work.json, served for api.crossref.org/works? and 404 for everything else)
_columns.expect: the result: ok + state + outcome, or ok=false + the refusal code

rows.why: the shape that always worked, kept as the control: a strict DOI regex that rejected real DOIs would show up here first.

an arXiv id is its OWN scheme, not a DOI. The hunted form carries the `arXiv:` prefix and a `v2` the stored identifier does not, so this also proves hunt's normaliser and litkb.norm_identifier('arxiv', ...) agree — a reference that normalised differently would miss the work and be admitted a second time.

the web-source path, end to end minus the GPU: fetched, shape-checked, filed under the work key and admitted as a manual PROPOSAL. extract=false stops before GROBID/Docling, which no unit test may run.
a URL whose shape is fine and whose BYTES are not. The reference validation must not swallow this: it is a different refusal, made later, on the bytes (the 2026-09-15 incident, row H1).

rows.ref: Progress in Statistics: European Meeting of Statisticians, Budapest, 1972, Vols I and II.
rows.why: the new scheme, and the handoff that makes it work: the title goes through gate 0 (resolve_doi -> RESOLVE_TITLE_RATIO -> first-author family -> year) and the DOI it returns is what the ladder looks up. `ref_kind` stays 'title' -- that is what the REFERENCE is -- and the DOI appears under `resolved`. This row quotes the frozen candidate's title EXACTLY, so its ratio is 1.00 and RESOLVE_TITLE_RATIO is untouched; the same frozen response with a NEAR title (ratio 0.83) is refused by test_a_wrong_work_scoring_just_under_the_ratio_is_refused. One response, both sides of the gate.

rows.ref: Progress in Statistics: European Meeting of Statisticians, Budapest, 1972.
rows.why: gate 0 judges on title AND first-author family AND year. Without the surname every candidate is refused for a reason that has nothing to do with the title, and the hunt would report `ambiguous-title` for a reference that was never resolvable. The refusal NAMES the missing flag instead.

rows.ref: Progress in Statistics: European Meeting of Statisticians, Budapest, 1972.
rows.why: the other half. A title with no year accepts a sibling edition as readily as the work, and litkb does not guess a year.

rows.ref: An Entirely Unfindable Monograph On Nothing In Particular
rows.why: gate 0 saw NO candidate at all (every registry answered 404). That is a different problem from a candidate the gate refused, and the next move is a better title -- so it gets its own code rather than being folded into `ambiguous-title`.

rows.ref: Recent Progress in Statistics: European Meeting of Statisticians, Budapest.
rows.why: the SAME frozen response as the `title` row, queried with a near-title instead of the exact one: the candidate scores 0.83, gate 0 refuses it, and the hunt says a candidate was found and refused rather than pretending none existed. This is the identity gate seen from inside hunt() -- test_a_wrong_work_scoring_just_under_the_ratio_is_refused is the same refusal seen at resolve_doi.

(c) item 2. A scheme litkb RECORDS and a hunt cannot follow is a RESULT that says so and names who owns it (S3) -- never a traceback, and never an attempt to confirm an ISBN at Crossref as if it were a DOI. `ref_kind` is null because nothing was validated as huntable; the scheme that WAS recognised comes back as `ref_scheme`, so a caller can tell 'litkb has no route for this' from 'litkb has never heard of this'.

(c) item 1, and the whole reason ref_kind stopped classifying. This string used to be called a DOI, handed to admit_registry and killed with AdmissionError('... is not a DOI'). It is now a named refusal, and `ref_kind` is null rather than a guess.
